learning_outcomes.text: Capacity to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of the degree.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to organize and plan resources and people in the business, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Adopt a responsible, orderly attitude to work, and open to learning, considering the challenge posed by the necessary continuous training.
Apply the strategies of the scientific methodology: analyze the problematic situation qualitatively and quantitatively, propose hypotheses and solutions using engineering models.
Work effectively in a group, integrating capabilities and knowledge to make decisions in the field of professional practice linked to the degree.

syllabus_topics: Formation 1: Introduction to the "Company in the University": structure, work groups, roles and responsibilities, communication mechanisms, alignment with SDGs, standardized work procedures, and quality assurance mechanisms.
Formation 2a: Safety training (Workshop): workshop work; risk prevention and procedures in case of accident.
Formation 2b: Safety training (Electrical): work with electrical systems; risk prevention and procedures in case of accident.
Formation 4: Waste management and sustainability of manufacturing processes.
Activity 2: Conceptual design of a subsystem with sustainability, cost, and manufacturing considerations.

assessment_methods.method: Assistance and use of all training activities
Assistance and use in project development activities
Assistance and use of STEAM promotion activities

assessment_rules: It will be an essential condition to pass the course to obtain at least 50% from the sum of the evaluation mechanisms described. This pilot course is in a Challenge-Based Learning format, so continuous assessment cannot be waived due to its nature. The student will be considered to have waived the evaluation if they do not submit the assigned project or stop attending project monitoring and tutoring meetings, in which case they will be considered to have opted to abandon the pilot itinerary. For the extraordinary call, the same evaluation and waiver mechanisms as the ordinary call apply.
